subject: Oceanography
title: Antarctic Bottom Water
description: A quick, practical guide to Antarctic Bottom Water.

hook.text: The coldest, densest water on Earth forms along Antarctica's coast—then slides to the bottom of every ocean.

buildup.text: When sea ice forms, it rejects salt—making the surrounding water extremely cold and salty.

discovery.text: This dense water sinks to the abyss and flows northward—ventilating the deep ocean with oxygen.

twist.text: Antarctic Bottom Water reaches as far as the North Atlantic—a journey that takes over a thousand years.

climax.text: If its formation slows—as warming suggests—deep oceans could become oxygen-depleted.

punchline.text: Antarctic water fills the deepest floors of every ocean on Earth.

quiz.question: How does Antarctic Bottom Water form?
options: Sea ice formation rejects salt, making cold salty water sink
